newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala defends distance from ACPC export quotas.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala defends distance from ACPC export quotas.

text.p: The National Coffee Association (Anacafe) defended Wednesday its "freedom of choice" in not joining the coffee export limit plan of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC).
"We believe that every person or country has the right to choose when to sell or buy their coffee," Julio Arrivillaga, the new president of Anacafe, told Reuters.

Arrivillaga was responding to comments made earlier this month by Colombian Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo, who said Guatemala and Mexico, neither participants in the export plan, were a destabilizing force in coffee markets.
ACPC's program is designed to control export flows from producer nations in a bid to bolster world coffee prices.

Guatemala participated in the plan during the 1993-1994 harvest, but has not limited its exports since then "due in part to inconsistencies and irregularities from more than one of the most important coffee producers," said Arrivillaga.
According to Arrivillaga the plan has only short-term benefits in upholding artificial prices.
Arrivillaga denied Mexico and Guatemala have joined forces to boycott the ACPC. He said each country was acting independently.
